Abdus Sobhan Sheikh ------ Petitioner
vs
Kazi Moulana Jabedullah and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued at the instance of the pre-emptor in a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against the judgment and order dated 24-6-96 passed in Misc. Appeal 4 of 1992 by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Bagerhat affirming the judgment and order dated 22-1-92 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986, by the Senior Assistant Judge Bagerhat disallowing the prayer for pre-emption, of the present petitioner who is admittedly a co-sharer in the case holding. 

 2. The petitioner filed the Original pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 67 of 1987 on 19-8-85 under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act because the land under pre-emption is a part of the homestead. But the disputed land is situated beyond municipal area. The transfer was completed under section 60 of the Registration Act on 20-6-85. The application for pre-emption was filed within 120 days ie within the period of limitation. The pre-emptee filed written objection contending inter alia, that since the land under pre, emption was not within the municipal area the pre-emption case should have been filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, Therefore the pre-emptor came up with an application for amendment of the plaint of the pre-emption case. The amendment application was filed on 4-11-89. That was allowed on 5-11-89 converting the pre-emption case under section 96 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. According to section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act, the pre-emptor deposited the entire consideration money and 5% compensation on it and accordingly, the present petitioner preemptor deposited an amount of Taka 1250.00 as compensation. The total deposit was Taka 26,250.00 made before filing of the case. After the case was converted under section 960f the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as per amendment, the pre-emptor was required to make deposit of further 5% compensation that is to make the deposit of compensation @ 10% being further Taka 1250.00 as was required under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, The deposit was made on 5-11-89 after the said amendment. Against the said amendment both as to conversion of the case and for depositing the additional compensation the pre-emptee did not raise any objection and did not move higher forum. 

 3. The ground for pre-emption of the pre-emptor principally is that he is a co-sharer and the purchaser is a stranger and without giving notice under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the sale was made. The pre-emption case was however filed within time. On contest the trial Court dismissed the pre-emption case on the ground that the case was bad for defect of party finding that one Obaidul Hoque was not made party in the pre-emption proceeding. 

 6. As it is found so far the question of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence is concerned, no issue was framed in the trial Court as no specific allegation was made in the written objection filed by the pre-emptor in the trial Court. In this deposition the DW 1 the pre-emptee has only stated that the pre-emptor was present at the time of execution and registration of the deed of sale in question in the office of the sub-registrar. But this lone statement judgment has not been corroborated by any other witness or evidence. 

 Another moot question in this case is whether in a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act if the consideration money and part of the compensation is paid or deposited within the statutory period of the limitation being 120 days and another part of compensation only is deposited later on after statutory period but on amendment of the pre-emption application as stated above the case becomes barred by limitation or not. 

 "Amendment of pleadings under Order 7 rule 17 CPC special limitation prescribed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the question of limitation may arise in two cases (i) whether the claim to be included was barred on the date of institution of the suit (ii) whether the claim is barred on the date of the prayer for amendment. In this case the amendment will-relate back to the date of the institution of the case". 

 9. Mr Ashfaqul Islam, the learned Counsel for the pre-emptor petitioner cites another decision. It is in the case of Selina Begum and another vs Mofizul Islam and others, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 77 also wherein the judgment was pronounced by his Lordship Mr Badrul Haider Chowdhury J. That case was also under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the question arose whether the balance of consideration money can be deposited beyond four months. In para 5 of the said decision their Lordships have held' as under: 

 10. In the instant case it is found that the pre-emptor at first filed the case under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act and the deposit was made of the consideration money and 5% of the same compensation. After conversion of the case under section 96 of the State' Acquisition find Tenancy Act the defect was detected as to deposit of balance of 5% of the compensation. The balance amount was deposited as per order of the trial Court granting amendment application and as such, deposit can be treated and accepted as valid deposit which was made after the amendment of the pre-emption application and the amendment since relates back to the date of filing of the pre-emption case which was made in time, the case, is not barred by limitation. In the case of Md Mofizuddin Sarker vs Md Abdul Jabbar Akhand, reported in 1 BLD 486 which is a Single Bench decision, it has been held that if the application is made within the period of limitation and the consideration money is also deposited in court within the period of limitation, it shall be deemed that the deposit has been made while making the application for pre-emption under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (XXVIII) of 1951 s 96(3 ) (a) (para 2) So the provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, wherein it has been stated that the deposit of the consideration money along with 10% compensation shall accompany the pre-emption, application, in view of the said decision. I find that the time for deposit has been relaxed and extended. So the principle as to deposit is not rigid and it is not mandatory that the entire deposit both the consideration money and compensation should be paid before filing of the case. Moreover, in the instant case the deposit of consideration money along with 5% of the compensation was made in time and it accompanied the petition of pre-emption. Only balance of 5% compensation was deposited after amendment. 

 11. In the case of Akteruzzaman vs Habilullah 31 DLR (AD) 88 (para 28) it has been held that deposit of entire consideration along with 10% compensation for pre-condition must be deposited when the pre-emption application is filed, in compliance of sub-section 3 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. There is some distinction in that case and the instant case. In that the pre-emptor himself made the proportionate deposit by calculating himself later on he made the deposit of the balance amount as per order of the High Court Division, so prayer for preemption was refused in that case by the Appellate Division on the ground of limitation. But in the instant case entire consideration money along with 5% of compensation was deposited before filing of the pre-emption application under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act and after amendment was allowed for converting the case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the remaining 5% of the compensation was deposited since the order of amendment relating back to the date of filing of the case the instant case does not become barred by limitation as it was filed originally within the statutory period of 120 days. 

 12. Under the circumstances of this case it is found that the learned Counsel who filed the original pre-emption case being confused because of the fact that the case land comprising part of homestead and as such the original application was filed under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act and later on rectification was made by way of amendment of the plaint of the pre-emption case converting it into under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 14. The whole framework of the law of pre-emption both under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has been made with the purpose and intention to check the infiltrators from outside come within a holding enjoyed by its co-sharers.
